title: Hidden among the baggage (1 Samuel 10:20–24)
hook: the tall new king hides from his own crowning

segments.voice: Yesterday, the elders asking Samuel for a king, like all the nations. Your line was take, and take, and take. Today, they get their king, if they can find him.

The whole people is gathered at Mizpah, and Samuel names a king by lot, so everyone can watch it narrow down. The tribes come near, and the tribe of Benjamin is taken. Then the family of the Matrites. Then one man: Saul, the son of Kish. Every eye turns to find him, and he isn't there. They look. They call. Nothing. So they ask the LORD: has the man come here yet? And the answer comes back: "Behold, he hath hid himself among the baggage."
screen: `BENJAMIN IS TAKEN.` → `SAUL, SON OF KISH.` → `AND HE ISN'T THERE.`

segments.voice: Here's what makes it strange: Saul already knows. Samuel had taken him aside on the edge of town, poured oil on his head, and told him God had chosen him. When Saul went home and his uncle asked what Samuel had said, Saul told him about the lost donkeys he'd been chasing, and nothing about the kingdom. And before any of that, when Samuel first hinted at it, Saul said: am I not a Benjamite, of the smallest of the tribes of Israel, and isn't my family the least of them all? Gideon said much the same, down in his winepress. So the lot can hardly surprise him. And he's hiding among the gear, the bags and supplies people brought. The tallest man in Israel, crouched behind the luggage. The people run and fetch him, and when he stands among them, he's higher than any of them from his shoulders upward. Samuel says: do you see the one the LORD has chosen? There's none like him. The people shout: long live the king. But not everyone. Some worthless men say, how shall this man save us? They despise him and bring him no gift. And Saul, the text says, held his peace. Readers hear his hiding in different ways: humility, a man who didn't want power, or fear, a man who knew how heavy it would be. The text doesn't decide. It shows a man who looked like a king from the outside, crouched where no one could see him.
screen: `ANOINTED IN SECRET, TOLD NO ONE.` · `THE SMALLEST OF THE TRIBES.` · `THE TALLEST MAN, BEHIND THE BAGS.` · `HOW SHALL THIS MAN SAVE US?` · then, large: `HE HATH HID HIMSELF AMONG THE BAGGAGE.`

segments.voice: Think of something you've been asked to do, or know you're meant to do, that you keep ducking, leading something, speaking up, being the grown-up in a hard family moment, and notice where you've been hiding: busyness, jokes, the luggage. Don't force a decision; just stand up from behind the bags in your mind, and let yourself be seen. If you pray, ask for the strength to stand.
Saul. The tall new king, already anointed in secret, found hiding among the baggage when the lot fell on him at Mizpah.
Your line: he hid among the baggage. Even the tallest man can hide. That's day seven hundred thirty-two.

howItsDone: Jews read Saul's choosing at Mizpah as part of the Former Prophets; commentators differ on whether his hiding shows humility or fear.

notes: Audit: cut 'almost like a smile' (puts a tone on God's answer the text doesn't give) and 'from the inside wanted to disappear' (an inner state the text, which 'doesn't decide', never states).
Verify JPS 1917 wording of 10:22 (the KJV has 'among the stuff'; the index uses 'baggage', the JPS word).
'Long live the king' (10:24) is given without quotation marks; the KJV has 'God save the king'. Confirm the JPS 1917 wording if it is to be quoted.
'The tallest man in Israel' rests on 10:23 (higher than any of the people) and 9:2; confirm the phrasing is fair.
'Worthless men' paraphrases 10:27 (KJV 'children of Belial'); 'held his peace' follows the KJV.
Humility vs. fear readings are attributed to 'readers' and not ranked.
Original: הַכֵּלִים, as in 10:22 ('el-hakelim'); confirm vocalization.
